q: What are Mumbai's lunchbox delivery workers, famous for their near error-free system, called?
note: Prince Charles met them in Mumbai in 2003 and later invited them to his wedding.

q: Mumbai's curving Marine Drive promenade is popularly nicknamed what?
note: At night its streetlights look like a string of pearls from Malabar Hill.

q: Which Mumbai arch monument was built to commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary?
note: It was completed in 1924, and the last British troops left India through it in 1948.

q: Which Mumbai art district, whose name means 'black horse', hosts a famous annual arts festival?
note: The name refers to a statue of King Edward VII on a black horse, removed in 1965.

q: What is Mumbai's huge open-air laundry beside Mahalaxmi station, where washermen scrub clothes in concrete pens, called?
note: Thousands of clothes are washed, dried and ironed there every single day.

q: Which beach at the northern end of Marine Drive is a favourite spot for Ganesh idol immersions?
note: It's a classic evening hangout for gola, kulfi and sea breeze.

q: Before 1996, Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus was named after which monarch?
note: Designed by architect F. W. Stevens, the station building was completed in 1888.

q: Which Mumbai Ganesh idol is famously called the 'Navsacha Ganpati', the wish-fulfilling Ganesha?
note: The mandal that installs it was founded in 1934 in the Lalbaug market area.

q: Which freedom fighter is credited with popularising Ganeshotsav as a big public festival in the 1890s?
note: Before this, Ganesh Chaturthi was mostly celebrated privately at home.

q: At the end of Ganeshotsav, crowds chant 'Ganpati Bappa ___'. Fill in the blank.
note: The chant continues 'Pudhchya varshi lavkar ya', asking him to return soon next year.

q: In Marathi, what does 'Aamchi Mumbai' mean?
note: The phrase is a proud everyday way Mumbaikars talk about their city.

q: Which nickname for Mumbai is also the title of Suketu Mehta's 2004 non-fiction book?
note: The book was a finalist for the 2005 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction.

q: Mumbai's beloved 'Bombay duck' is not a bird at all. What is it?
note: Locally called bombil, it is often served fried in a crisp rava coating.

q: Which Mumbai suburban line runs from CSMT to Panvel via Vashi?
note: Mumbai's suburban network also includes the Western and Central lines.

q: Mumbai's classic black-and-yellow taxis, the last of which retired in 2023, were which car model?
note: Mumbaikars call black-and-yellow cabs 'kaali-peeli'.

q: What does BEST, the organisation that runs Mumbai's red buses, stand for?
note: Besides buses, BEST also supplies electricity to the island city of Mumbai.

q: Mumbai's old Irani cafés are famous for bun maska served with which drink?
note: Kyani & Co., opened in 1904, is one of the oldest Irani cafés still running.

q: Bombay passed to England in 1661 as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry when she married which king?
note: The Crown leased it to the East India Company in 1668 for just £10 a year.

q: What was Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya museum formerly called?
note: Its foundation stone was laid by the future King George V in 1905.

q: Which Mumbai company, founded in 1897, began by making locks?
note: Godrej also built independent India's first indigenous typewriter in 1955.

q: Which Goan cartoonist's crowded, witty drawings cover the walls of Café Mondegar in Mumbai?
note: He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 2012.

q: Which ancient Buddhist rock-cut caves lie inside Mumbai's Sanjay Gandhi National Park?
note: Kanheri has over 100 rock-cut caves, some dating to around the 1st century BCE.

q: In Marathi, what does 'Aai' mean?
note: A father is commonly called 'Baba' in Marathi.

q: Puran poli, a sweet Maharashtrian flatbread, is stuffed with chana dal cooked with which sweetener?
note: It is usually served with a generous spoon of ghee on top.

q: Tambda rassa is a fiery red mutton broth. What is its milder white, coconut-based counterpart called?
note: 'Rassa' simply means a thin curry or broth in Marathi.

q: Which hill station between Mumbai and Pune is famous for its chikki?
note: The ancient Buddhist Karla and Bhaja caves are close to the town.

q: Which Maharashtra city gives its name to a famous handcrafted leather chappal?
note: These chappals received a GI tag in 2019, shared between Maharashtra and Karnataka.

q: Saoji cuisine, known for its fiery dark curries, is most associated with which city?
note: Saoji curries are typically mutton or chicken in a thin, fiery, dark gravy.

q: Pune's Chitale Bandhu is famous for which crispy spiral snack filled with coconut, sesame and spices?
note: The dough is made from gram flour and rolled up like a pinwheel before frying.

q: Sabudana khichdi, a popular fasting dish in Maharashtra, is made mainly from what?
note: It is usually cooked with crushed roasted peanuts, cumin and green chillies.

q: Which Maharashtra city is often called India's wine capital?
note: Sula Vineyards released its first wines from there in 2000.

q: The Ajanta Caves are especially celebrated for which kind of art?
note: A British hunting party led by officer John Smith came upon them in 1819.

q: Which Maharashtra tomb, built by Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah, is nicknamed the 'Taj of the Deccan'?
note: It honours Aurangzeb's wife, Dilras Banu Begum.

q: Which Pune palace-fortress was built as the seat of Peshwa Bajirao I in the 1730s?
note: Its foundation was laid on a Saturday in 1730, hence 'Shaniwar' in the name.

q: In which Pune palace was Mahatma Gandhi interned during the Quit India Movement?
note: It was built in 1892 by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III.

q: Which car-free Maharashtra hill station is reached by a narrow-gauge toy train from Neral?
note: British official Hugh Malet is credited with 'discovering' it in 1850.

q: Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra is especially famous for growing which fruit?
note: The Krishna river is traditionally said to rise at Mahabaleshwar.

q: Which Indian city is popularly called the 'Oxford of the East'?
note: It was the seat of the powerful Peshwas in the 18th century.

q: Who, with her husband Jyotirao, opened a school for girls in Pune in 1848?
note: She is widely remembered as one of India's first women teachers.

q: Dadasaheb Phalke, the father of Indian cinema, was born in Trimbak, near which Maharashtra city?
note: Phalke's full name was Dhundiraj Govind Phalke.

q: Which beloved Marathi humorist and writer is known simply as 'Pu La'?
note: His character sketch collection 'Vyakti Ani Valli' is a Marathi classic.

q: Marathi Language Day, 27 February, marks the birthday of which poet?
note: He won the Jnanpith Award, India's top literary honour, in 1987.

q: Anandibai Joshi of Kalyan, among the first Indian women doctors of Western medicine, graduated in 1886 in which country?
note: She studied at the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania.

q: At which hill fort above Junnar was Chhatrapati Shivaji born?
note: Shivaji is said to be named after the goddess Shivai, whose temple stands inside the fort.

q: Which sea fort off Malvan was built by Shivaji in the 1660s?
note: A handprint and footprint said to be Shivaji's are preserved inside it.

q: The annual Wari foot pilgrimage in Maharashtra ends at which temple town?
note: Pilgrims called warkaris walk for around three weeks during the monsoon.

q: Which 13th-century Marathi saint wrote a famous commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, completed around 1290?
note: The work, the Dnyaneshwari, is one of the earliest great texts of Marathi literature.

q: Sant Tukaram, the 17th-century Marathi saint-poet, came from which village near Pune?
note: His devotional songs are called abhangs.

q: Pola, a farmers' festival of Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, honours which animals?
note: Farmers bathe and decorate them, and the animals rest from work that day.

q: Apart from Paithan itself, which Maharashtra town is the biggest centre of Paithani saree weaving?
note: Traditional Paithanis are woven in pure silk with zari, often with peacock borders.

q: Which Maharashtra city is famous for its GI-tagged cotton bedsheets called chaddars?
note: The city's terry towels also carry a GI tag.

q: What is the Marathi name of Maharashtra's state bird, the yellow-footed green pigeon?
note: These pigeons are often seen feeding in flocks on fig trees.

q: The Koli dance of Maharashtra's coast reflects the life of which workers?
note: Dancers mimic rowing boats and casting nets.

q: Shrikhand, a sweet Maharashtrian and Gujarati dessert, is made from strained what?
note: Add mango pulp and it becomes amrakhand.

q: Sol kadhi, the pink Konkan drink, is made from kokum and what?
note: It is often served after a spicy Malvani meal to cool the stomach.

q: Locho, a soft, spicy steamed gram-flour snack, originated in which Gujarat city?
note: 'Locho' is Gujarati slang for a mix-up, a nod to its famously mushy texture.

q: Ghari, a rich ghee-and-mawa sweet eaten on Chandani Padvo, is a speciality of which city?
note: Chandani Padvo falls the day after Sharad Purnima.

q: In Gujarat, fafda with jalebi is the traditional breakfast on which festival day?
note: Fafda is served with fried green chillies and a raw papaya relish called sambharo.

q: Which soft Gujarati flatbread, often made with fenugreek leaves, is a favourite food for long train journeys?
note: Theplas stay fresh for days, which makes them perfect travel food.

q: Which thin, crisp, roasted Gujarati flatbread comes in flavours like methi and jeera?
note: It is roasted slowly on a griddle while being pressed flat with a cloth.

q: Dabeli, the spicy potato-filled bun, originated in which region of Gujarat?
note: 'Dabeli' means 'pressed' in Gujarati.

q: Which square in old Ahmedabad is a jewellery market by day and a buzzing food street by night?
note: Its late-night stalls are known for chocolate sandwiches and pav bhaji.

q: Gujarat's Wagh Bakri tea brand is headquartered in which city?
note: Its logo shows a tiger and a goat sharing a cup of tea.

q: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat depicts which leader?
note: It stands on Sadhu Bet island, facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

q: Adalajni Vav, near Ahmedabad, is what kind of structure?
note: Completed in the late 1490s, it is five storeys deep and kept travellers cool.

q: Which Gujarat stepwell appears on the back of the lavender ₹100 note introduced in 2018?
note: It was built in the 11th century in Patan in memory of King Bhima I.

q: The stone 'tree of life' lattice of which Ahmedabad mosque inspired IIM Ahmedabad's logo?
note: The mosque was built in 1573.

q: In which Gujarat city is the Laxmi Vilas Palace, often described as four times the size of Buckingham Palace?
note: Construction began in 1878 and the palace was completed in 1890.

q: In which Gujarat coastal town was Mahatma Gandhi born?
note: His ancestral home there is now a memorial called Kirti Mandir.

q: The Sun Temple at Modhera, Gujarat, was built under which dynasty?
note: The Solankis are also called the Chaulukyas; the temple dates to 1026-27 under King Bhima I.

q: Gujarat's Rann Utsav tent city is set up near which village, gateway to the White Rann?
note: The UN World Tourism Organization named it a Best Tourism Village in 2023.

q: Rogan art, painted with a thick castor-oil paste, is kept alive almost entirely by one family in which Gujarat village?
note: The paste is trailed from a metal stick that never touches the cloth.

q: The name of Gujarat's tie-dye craft Bandhani comes from a Sanskrit word meaning what?
note: Jamnagar and Bhuj are well known Bandhani centres.

q: Surat is a major centre for which metallic thread used in saree borders and embroidery?
note: Traditional zari was made by winding fine silver or gold wire around silk thread.

q: Which 1976 Shyam Benegal film about Gujarat's dairy cooperatives was funded by about 5 lakh farmers giving ₹2 each?
note: Girish Karnad, Smita Patil and Naseeruddin Shah starred in it.

q: Which 15th-century Gujarati poet-saint wrote 'Vaishnav Jan To', Gandhi's favourite bhajan?
note: He is often called the Adi Kavi, or first poet, of Gujarati.

q: Jamsetji Tata was born in 1839 in which Gujarat town?
note: Navsari has long been an important centre of India's Parsi community.

q: Which Gujarati poet, who collected Saurashtra's folk songs and tales, was called 'Rashtriya Shayar' by Gandhi?
note: His collection 'Saurashtra ni Rasdhar' preserved dozens of local folk tales.

q: Which Gujarati folk dance is performed in pairs with small decorated sticks?
note: The sticks are often said to represent the swords of Goddess Durga.

q: Which Gujarati folk dance sees women beat the floor with long wooden sticks while singing?
note: It began among women workers pounding lime into floors near Chorwad.

q: Gujarat's Tarnetar Fair is famous for colourfully embroidered what, carried by young men?
note: The fair is linked to the legend of Arjuna winning Draupadi's hand.

q: What does Gujarati script lack that Devanagari has?
note: Gandhi wrote his autobiography in Gujarati.

q: What does the Gujarati greeting 'Kem cho?' mean?
note: A common happy reply is 'Majama', meaning 'all good'.

q: In Gujarati, names are often followed by 'ben' for women. What does 'ben' mean?
note: Men's names often take 'bhai', meaning brother.

q: Gujaratis often say 'Aavjo' when someone leaves. What does it roughly mean?
note: It's used just like 'goodbye', but with a warm invitation to return.

q: Balaji Wafers, the popular chips brand, is based in which Gujarat city?
note: Its founder started out selling snacks at a cinema canteen.

q: Which Gujarat city was nicknamed the 'Manchester of India' for its textile mills?
note: Its first textile mill opened in 1861.

q: What is the Gujarati New Year, the day after Diwali, called?
note: People greet each other with 'Saal Mubarak' on the day.

q: What are the old gated residential neighbourhoods of Ahmedabad's walled city called?
note: Many have a chabutro, a tall ornate bird feeder, in their common square.

q: Goa's feni is distilled either from cashew apples or from what?
note: Cashew feni received a GI tag in 2009.

q: Goan vindaloo gets its name from a Portuguese dish of meat cooked with wine and what?
note: Goans swapped the wine for local palm vinegar.

q: What are Goa's traditional bread sellers, who cycle through villages every morning, called?
note: They announce themselves with a honk of a squeeze-bulb horn.

q: Which fun-loving king rules over the Goa Carnival each year?
note: The carnival is held just before the Christian season of Lent.

q: Which spring festival in Goa, celebrated around Holi, features float parades and folk dancers?
note: Folk troupes perform dances like ghode modni, a mock horse dance.

q: During Goa's São João festival, young men famously jump into what?
note: The festival honours St John the Baptist every 24 June.

q: Bonderam, a flag festival with playful mock fights, is held on which Goan island?
note: The flags recall how village property boundaries were marked in Portuguese times.

q: Old Goa's Basilica of Bom Jesus holds the remains of which saint?
note: His relics are put on public display roughly once a decade.

q: What is Panaji's colourful Portuguese-era Latin Quarter called?
note: Its narrow lanes are lined with brightly painted houses and overhanging balconies.

q: Which North Goa beach is famous for its Wednesday flea market?
note: The market grew out of the hippie gatherings of the late 1960s and 70s.

q: Which North Goa beach is often called the 'Queen of Beaches'?
note: It is Goa's biggest beach town, next to Baga.

q: Fort Aguada in Goa got its name from what it supplied to passing ships?
note: 'Aguada' means watering place in Portuguese.

q: Which river runs along Panaji's waterfront, where floating casino boats are moored?
note: Fort Aguada stands guard near the mouth of this river.

q: Which sport is hugely popular in Goa, with famous clubs like Dempo and Salgaocar?
note: FC Goa has played in the Indian Super League since its first season in 2014.

q: Which large wild bovine, also called the Indian bison, is Goa's state animal?
note: Gaur are the largest wild cattle species in the world.

q: What is the Konkani name for Goa's everyday meal of rice with fish curry?
note: In Konkani, xitt means cooked rice and kodi means curry.

q: Which hilltop fort above Goa's Vagator beach became a Bollywood landmark after a 2001 film?
note: The fort overlooks the mouth of the river that shares its name.

q: What are the blue-and-white painted ceramic tiles seen on Goa's Portuguese-era buildings called?
note: The word is often traced to an Arabic term for 'polished stone'.

q: In Konkani, what does 'Dev borem korum' mean?
note: Literally it means 'May God do you good'.

q: The Goan word 'susegad' describes what?
note: It comes from the Portuguese 'sossegado', meaning quiet or calm.

q: Which Indore food street's name literally means '56 shops'?
note: Its Johny Hot Dog stall has a cult following among Indoris.

q: Bhutte ka kees, grated corn cooked with milk and spices, is a street favourite of which city?
note: It is finished with lemon, coriander and grated coconut.

q: Which Madhya Pradesh town gives its name to a famous spicy, clove-scented sev?
note: Besides cloves, it gets its kick from black pepper.

q: Which Madhya Pradesh city is nicknamed the 'City of Lakes'?
note: Its Upper Lake, Bhojtal, is traditionally credited to the 11th-century king Raja Bhoj.

q: Which Madhya Pradesh hilltop fort is often called 'the pearl among the fortresses of India'?
note: A 9th-century inscription in its Chaturbhuj temple has one of the oldest known zeros.

q: Orchha, the old Bundela capital famous for its riverside chhatris, stands on which river?
note: The Jahangir Mahal there was built to welcome Mughal emperor Jahangir.

q: Mandu's famous love legend is about Sultan Baz Bahadur and which singer?
note: Her hilltop pavilion looks out over the Narmada valley.

q: Mandu's Jahaz Mahal gets its name because it looks like what?
note: It sits between two lakes, so it appears to float on water.

q: The Khajuraho temples were built by which dynasty?
note: Only around 25 of an estimated 85 original temples survive.

q: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was first commissioned by which emperor?
note: Its four richly carved gateways, called toranas, were added later.

q: Ancient Indian astronomers used which Madhya Pradesh city as their prime meridian?
note: The Tropic of Cancer also passes very close to the city.

q: Which hand block-printing craft is named after a small town in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar district?
note: It uses natural dyes, mainly red and black, on white cloth.

q: Revolutionary Chandra Shekhar Azad was born in Bhavra, a village in which present-day state?
note: The village was renamed Chandrashekhar Azad Nagar in his honour.

q: Maihar in Madhya Pradesh is linked with which sarod legend, guru of Ravi Shankar?
note: He also formed the Maihar Band, an orchestra of local musicians.

q: Which legendary playback singer was born in Indore in 1929?
note: Her father, Deenanath Mangeshkar, was a classical singer and stage actor.

q: Which legendary singer-actor was born in Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh?
note: As he had wished, his last rites were performed in Khandwa.

q: Which Madhya Pradesh district is home to the Majhgawan diamond mine?
note: Locals can lease small plots there to dig for diamonds themselves.

q: Bhedaghat's famous Marble Rocks gorge on the Narmada is near which city?
note: Nearby Dhuandhar Falls is named for its smoke-like spray, 'dhuan' meaning smoke.

q: Teejan Bai is a legendary performer of which Chhattisgarh folk ballad form?
note: It retells stories from the Mahabharata, usually centred on Bhima.

q: Which tussar-type silk, woven around Champa, is Chhattisgarh famous for?
note: Its silkworms feed on the leaves of trees like arjun and saja.

q: Which state is called the 'Rice Bowl of Central India'?
note: Locally the state is lovingly called 'Dhan ka Katora', a bowl of paddy.

q: Bore basi, a summer staple in Chhattisgarh, is cooked rice soaked overnight in what?
note: It is usually eaten with raw onion, green chilli and pickle.

q: The Laxman Temple at Sirpur, Chhattisgarh, is a famous early temple built from what material?
note: It dates to around the 7th century CE.

q: Which Chhattisgarh temple is nicknamed the 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh'?
note: It stands near Kawardha, at the foot of the Maikal hills.

q: What is Chhattisgarh's state animal?
note: The IUCN lists the wild water buffalo as endangered.

q: What is the state bird of Chhattisgarh?
note: It is a gifted mimic that can copy human speech.

q: The Bhilai Steel Plant in Chhattisgarh was set up with help from which country?
note: It has long supplied much of the rail used by Indian Railways.

q: Sua Nacha, a women's folk dance of Chhattisgarh, is named after which bird?
note: Dancers circle a basket holding a clay parrot while singing.

q: Mainpat, nicknamed the 'Shimla of Chhattisgarh', is known for its settlement of which people?
note: Tibetans settled on the plateau in the early 1960s.

q: Diu, the island off Gujarat's Saurashtra coast, was ruled for over four centuries by which European power?
note: Diu Fort was built after a 1535 treaty with Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.

q: Which maze of rock caves in Diu is loved by photographers for its shafts of sunlight?
note: The caves are thought to have been quarried for stone to build Diu Fort.

q: Diu is known for which unusual palm, rare in India, whose trunk splits into branches?
note: It is believed to have arrived from Africa during Portuguese times.

q: Which river divides Daman into Nani Daman and Moti Daman?
note: Moti Daman's old fort walls enclose Portuguese-era churches and offices.

q: In which year did Dadra and Nagar Haveli merge with Daman and Diu into one union territory?
note: Before the merger, the two were separate union territories.

q: In which year did Dadra and Nagar Haveli throw off Portuguese rule?
note: The territory is landlocked between Gujarat and Maharashtra.

q: Which horseshoe-shaped beach is Diu's most famous?
note: Its calm, sheltered waters are popular for swimming and water sports.

q: The tarpa, played at Warli dances in Dadra and Nagar Haveli, is what kind of instrument?
note: It is made from a dried gourd fitted with bamboo pipes.
